properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Broken stream cipher still shipped in the vendored BoringSSL: full RC4 implementation (e_rc4.cc) registered in the EVP cipher table (get_cipher.cc: EVP_rc4) and OID/NID tables. No application or Swift call site — Swift Crypto exposes only AEADs; RC4 remains reachable by any C consumer of CCryptoBoringSSL (legacy EVP users). Removed from every modern protocol; keystream biases make it broken outright. Changeable only by upstream BoringSSL sync.

properties.name: pqs:context

Reachable through the C EVP API and legacy PKCS#8 PBE paths; not exposed via Swift. No modern protocol uses it. Changeable only by upstream sync.

properties.name: pqs:context

Reachable by C consumers when reading decades-old PKCS#12 exports; not exposed via Swift. Weak block cipher, classically broken at export key lengths. Changeable only by upstream sync.

properties.name: pqs:context

Swift Crypto deliberately does not expose ECB among its AES modes (GCM/CBC/CTR/CFB/EAX/CCM are exposed; ECB would be C-API-only). Reachable by any consumer of CCryptoBoringSSL.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored BoringSSL internals, both password-related but neither a plaintext password store: (1) PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC_SHA1 — a salted, iterated PBKDF2 KDF using HMAC-SHA1, exported from the EVP API for PKCS#8/legacy interop; (2) SPAKE2's protocol-specified password-to-scalar step: a raw SHA-512 pre-hash of the password (spake25519.cc), by design of the PAKE, whose online rounds — not the hash — provide brute-force resistance. Available via the library C API; no Swift-level exposure.

Constant-time Poly1305 tag comparison in the open path. Classical-secure, Shor-irrelevant. Presence asset with full API exposure.
